claims.sql:
WITH p AS (SELECT model,mode,resolution,variate,wape pw FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND h=-1 AND candidate='point'),
     q AS (SELECT model,mode,resolution,variate,min(wape) qw,(array_agg(candidate ORDER BY wape))[1] bestq FROM provenance.forecast_metrics WHERE span='common' AND h=-1 AND candidate<>'point' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4)
SELECT model, count(*) FILTER (WHERE qw<pw) beats, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (qw-pw)/pw) FILTER (WHERE qw<pw) med,
  min((qw-pw)/pw) best FROM p JOIN q USING(model,mode,resolution,variate) GROUP BY 1;
-- and: SELECT bestq, count(*) ... WHERE model='timesfm' AND qw<pw GROUP BY 1;  -> p50:17, p10:1
claims.delta: 'modally p40' -> modally p50 (17/18); 'always by a below-median quantile' -> 17 of 18 wins are AT the median
claims.reasoning: The counts (18 of 20, 31 baseline cells), the median improvement (-1.68% -> -1.7%), the -45% extremum (-45.21%) and the p10 attribution for Holt-Winters on 1-s images are all exactly right. What is wrong is the quantile attribution for TimesFM: its point is the MEAN head and the winning candidate is the p50 (median) head in 17 of 18 cells, p30 in the one remaining cell -- p40 never wins a TimesFM cell. p40 IS the modal winner across all 51 cells (18 of them, all baseline cells), which is almost certainly where the number came from -- two different statistics were conflated. Note that p50 winning is exactly what the following sentence's explanation ('the conditional median already sits below the mean') predicts, so the correction strengthens the argument.
claims.proposed_fix: "TimesFM's mean head is beaten in 18 of its 20 cells (median improvement $-1.7\%$, always by the median or a lower quantile -- the p50 head in 17 of the 18, p30 in the last)".
